# Auto-generated rule: vi.restoreAllMocks() doesn't clear vi.fn() call-history from a vi.mock() factory

A vi.fn() instantiated inside a vi.mock('node:child_process', factory) factory (e.g. to stub execFileSync for a git-remote-layer Gap-3 test) keeps accumulating .mock.calls across sequential tests in the same file even with a file-level afterEach(() => vi.restoreAllMocks()). Symptom: a test asserting exec call count/args fails only when run as part of the full suite, passes in isolation (-t filter). Fix: explicitly execFileSync.mockClear() in a scoped beforeEach for the describe block(s) that assert on that mock's call history, rather than relying on the global restoreAllMocks.

## Evidence
tests/lib/autopilot/mr-draft.test.mjs Gap-3 describe blocks: 'derives the -R spec ... pins BOTH the list and create call' failed with 'expected [...4] to have a length of 1 but got 4' when run in the full file (86 passed/1 failed), passed in isolation (1/1). Root cause confirmed via -t "Gap 3" filter reproducing 4 accumulated calls = 1(first test)+2(second test)+1(own). Fix: added beforeEach(() => execFileSync.mockClear()) to both Gap-3 describe blocks; full file green (87/87) across 3 repeat runs.
